title: Shark Tank India: The Ultimate Pitch
description: Step into the Shark Tank! Pitch your startup to 5 legendary investors. Every shark has different priorities — convince them all or secure the deal of a lifetime. Your pitch, your valuation, your destiny.

scenes.title: Backstage at Shark Tank
scenes.narrative: You're in the green room at Film City, Mumbai. Your startup is about to be pitched on national TV. The makeup artist gives you a final touch-up while a producer clips a mic to your collar. Through the thin walls, you hear the muffled applause from the studio audience. You have 5 minutes before you walk through those famous doors. Last chance to prepare.
scenes.image_prompt: Nervous entrepreneur standing backstage in a green room at a TV studio in Mumbai, makeup mirrors with bright lights, a producer adjusting a microphone, Shark Tank India logo visible on a monitor, tense anticipation, cinematic lighting, vibrant illustration

choices.label: Review your financial projections
choices.description: Go through your revenue numbers, unit economics, and growth metrics one last time

choices.label: Practice your opening hook
choices.description: Rehearse your opening lines and presentation style in the mirror

scenes.title: The Numbers Game
scenes.narrative: You spread your financial sheets across the green room table. Revenue projections, unit economics, customer acquisition costs, lifetime value — the numbers that will make or break your pitch. Your co-founder sends a last-minute WhatsApp: 'The sharks will grill you on margins. Be ready.' You take a deep breath and focus.
scenes.image_prompt: Entrepreneur studying financial charts and spreadsheets on a tablet in a backstage green room, WhatsApp notification visible on phone, revenue graphs and pie charts glowing on screen, focused concentration, warm backstage lighting, detailed illustration

choices.label: Focus on profitability metrics
choices.description: Memorize your gross margins, EBITDA, and path to profitability

choices.label: Emphasize growth trajectory instead
choices.description: Highlight month-over-month growth, user acquisition, and market expansion

scenes.title: The Showman
scenes.narrative: You stand in front of the green room mirror, straightening your kurta. 'Namaste Sharks! My name is...' You try different energy levels — the excited founder, the confident CEO, the passionate innovator. Each version feels different. The floor manager peeks in: 'Two minutes!' Your heart races.
scenes.image_prompt: Entrepreneur rehearsing a pitch in front of a mirror in a TV studio green room, practicing different gestures and expressions, reflection showing confident pose, clock on wall showing time pressure, dramatic lighting, expressive illustration

choices.label: Go with high energy, Bollywood style
choices.description: Bring maximum enthusiasm and showmanship to your entrance

choices.label: Stay calm and data-driven
choices.description: Keep your composure and let the numbers do the talking

scenes.title: Walking Through The Doors
scenes.narrative: The floor manager gives you the signal. Your palms are sweaty. The iconic Shark Tank doors begin to open, and blinding studio lights flood your vision. As your eyes adjust, you see them — five sharks seated on their thrones, each worth hundreds of crores, each with the power to change your life. The studio audience falls silent. Cameras zoom in. This is it. The moment you've dreamed about, prepared for, and feared in equal measure. There is no turning back now.
scenes.image_prompt: Dramatic wide-angle shot of entrepreneur walking through the iconic Shark Tank doors into a brightly lit studio, five powerful investors seated on elevated chairs, studio cameras and audience visible, golden spotlight on the pitcher, cinematic and grand, Shark Tank India set design, vibrant illustration

npcs.name: Ananya Sharma
npcs.personality: Warm but sharp. Values branding, customer experience, and lifestyle appeal. She built a ₹500 crore lifestyle brand from scratch and knows what it takes to connect with Indian consumers emotionally.
npcs.domain_expertise: branding, consumer experience, D2C brands, lifestyle products, marketing strategy

npcs.name: Vikram Patel
npcs.personality: Analytical, data-obsessed. Loves tech-first solutions and scalable architectures. Former CTO of a unicorn who now invests in deep-tech and SaaS startups. Will grill you on tech stack and unit economics.
npcs.domain_expertise: technology, SaaS, AI/ML, scalable systems, data analytics

npcs.name: Priya Menon
npcs.personality: Practical, no-nonsense. Cares about margins and supply chain efficiency. Built a ₹1000 crore FMCG empire by obsessing over operations. If your numbers don't add up, she'll be the first to call it out.
npcs.domain_expertise: operations, supply chain, FMCG, retail distribution, manufacturing margins

npcs.name: Rajesh Gupta
npcs.personality: Old school, values hard work and grit. Looks for practical, Make-in-India solutions with real-world impact. Started from a small factory in Ludhiana and built a manufacturing conglomerate. Respects founders who get their hands dirty.
npcs.domain_expertise: manufacturing, B2B sales, exports, industrial products, Make-in-India initiatives

npcs.name: Deepa Iyer
npcs.personality: Aggressive, growth-at-all-costs. Wants 10x returns and billion-dollar outcomes. Runs one of India's top VC funds and has backed 5 unicorns. She thinks in multiples, not margins. If your TAM isn't big enough, she's out.
npcs.domain_expertise: venture capital, growth metrics, market sizing, competitive analysis, exits and IPOs

competitors.name: Arjun Kapoor
competitors.chat_personality: A charismatic competitor who pitched before you and set a high bar. Confident to the point of arrogance, he brags about his numbers and tries to psych you out. Uses aggressive valuation tactics and name-drops connections with the sharks.

base_rounds.title: The Opening Pitch
base_rounds.story: All eyes are on you. The five sharks lean forward in their seats. The studio lights feel hotter than you expected. You have 60 seconds to hook them with your opening pitch. The audience holds its breath. How you begin will set the tone for everything that follows.
base_rounds.goal: Deliver a compelling opening that captures the sharks' attention
base_rounds.image_prompt: Entrepreneur standing alone on the Shark Tank India stage under a bright spotlight, five investors leaning forward with intense curiosity, large screen behind showing a startup logo, audience silhouettes in background, dramatic TV studio lighting, cinematic wide shot illustration
base_rounds.timeout_feedback: You froze on camera! The sharks look unimpressed by your hesitation. A painful silence fills the studio before someone coughs.

choices.label: Lead with the problem statement
choices.description: Start by painting a vivid picture of the problem your product solves
choices.feedback: The sharks nod in unison. A problem-first approach always resonates — every great business starts with a real pain point.

choices.label: Lead with traction numbers
choices.description: Open with your impressive growth metrics and revenue figures
choices.feedback: Vikram's eyes light up at the numbers. Deepa scribbles notes furiously. Nothing speaks louder than traction in the tank.

choices.label: Lead with a product demo
choices.description: Pull out your product and let it speak for itself
choices.feedback: Rajesh leans in to examine the product closely. 'Interesting...' he murmurs. Priya picks it up to inspect the build quality.

choices.label: Lead with your personal story
choices.description: Share your emotional founding journey — the struggles, the sacrifices, the dream
choices.feedback: Ananya is visibly moved. Even Priya's tough expression softens. A great founder story creates an emotional anchor that data alone cannot.

base_rounds.title: The Interrogation
base_rounds.story: The sharks start firing questions from all directions. Priya wants to know your gross margins. Vikram drills into your tech stack. Deepa questions your valuation methodology. Rajesh asks about your manufacturing process. Ananya probes your brand positioning. It's a gauntlet, and every answer matters.
base_rounds.goal: Handle tough questions from the sharks without losing confidence
base_rounds.image_prompt: Five powerful investors firing rapid questions at an entrepreneur on the Shark Tank stage, speech bubbles with financial terms and question marks, entrepreneur standing firm under pressure, intense interrogation atmosphere, dramatic lighting with multiple angles, vibrant illustration

choices.label: Answer honestly, even uncomfortable truths
choices.description: Be transparent about weaknesses and challenges — the sharks will respect your honesty
choices.feedback: Your honesty earns respect across the panel. Rajesh nods approvingly — he's seen too many founders hide bad numbers. Trust is the currency of deal-making.

choices.label: Deflect with future projections
choices.description: Redirect tough questions toward your ambitious growth plans and future potential
choices.feedback: Deepa seems satisfied with the growth narrative, but Priya narrows her eyes. She's heard every deflection trick in the book.

choices.label: Use data and research to back every claim
choices.description: Pull out charts, studies, and benchmarks to support each answer with evidence
choices.feedback: Vikram is visibly impressed by your preparation. 'Finally, someone who comes with data!' he exclaims. The other sharks take note.

choices.label: Get emotional and passionate
choices.description: Let your genuine passion shine through — show the sharks how much this means to you
choices.feedback: Passion is a double-edged sword in the tank. Some sharks are moved, others wonder if emotion is masking weak fundamentals.

base_rounds.title: The Valuation Battle
base_rounds.story: Deepa Iyer leans forward and locks eyes with you. '₹1 Crore valuation. Walk me through what justifies this number,' she says, her voice cutting through the studio silence. The other sharks watch closely — your answer here will determine who stays in and who walks out.
base_rounds.goal: Defend or adjust your valuation strategically
base_rounds.image_prompt: Intense negotiation moment on Shark Tank India stage, a female VC investor pointing at a valuation number displayed on screen, entrepreneur defending their position with hand gestures, other sharks watching intently, split-screen tension, dramatic close-up lighting, cinematic illustration
base_rounds.timeout_feedback: Your silence speaks volumes. The sharks sense weakness in your hesitation. Deepa shakes her head slowly.

choices.label: Stand firm on valuation
choices.description: Defend every rupee of your valuation with conviction and data
choices.feedback: Deepa respects the confidence — she's seen too many founders crumble under pressure. But Priya thinks you're overvaluing and crosses her arms.

choices.label: Offer to negotiate
choices.description: Show flexibility by offering a valuation range and inviting counter-offers
choices.feedback: The sharks see you as reasonable and mature. Multiple sharks lean in — flexibility is a sign of a founder they can work with.

choices.label: Counter with milestone-based valuation
choices.description: Propose a lower valuation now with performance-based triggers that unlock higher value
choices.feedback: Vikram's eyes widen. 'Now we're talking!' he exclaims. A structured deal shows sophistication that most pitchers lack.

choices.label: Reveal a hidden trump card
choices.description: Drop a bombshell — a major partnership, LOI, or metric you've been strategically holding back
choices.feedback: Gasps in the tank! The sharks exchange excited glances. A well-timed reveal can completely shift the power dynamic in a negotiation.

base_rounds.title: Product Deep Dive
base_rounds.story: Rajesh stands up from his chair and walks toward you — something he rarely does. 'Show me the product,' he says. Ananya chimes in: 'I want to understand the customer experience end-to-end.' This is where your product either shines or crumbles under scrutiny.
base_rounds.goal: Demonstrate your product's value and market fit
base_rounds.image_prompt: Shark Tank investor standing up and walking toward an entrepreneur to examine a product up close, other investors watching with curiosity, product displayed on a table with spotlight, studio audience leaning forward, intimate product demonstration moment, detailed illustration

choices.label: Live product demonstration
choices.description: Fire up the product and show it working in real-time on stage
choices.feedback: The live demo is always the highest-risk, highest-reward move in the tank. Technology can be your best friend or your worst enemy on live TV.

choices.label: Show customer testimonials
choices.description: Play video testimonials from real customers who love your product
choices.feedback: Real customers' words carry more weight than any pitch deck. Ananya nods — she knows brand love when she sees it. Priya appreciates the social proof.

choices.label: Present competitive analysis
choices.description: Show a detailed breakdown of how you stack up against every competitor in the market
choices.feedback: The sharks appreciate that you know your competition inside and out. Deepa is particularly impressed — she invests based on competitive moats.

choices.label: Offer sharks a hands-on trial
choices.description: Hand the product to each shark and let them experience it firsthand
choices.feedback: Rajesh's face lights up as he tries the product himself! There's nothing more powerful than putting your product in an investor's hands. Vikram immediately starts testing edge cases.

base_rounds.title: The Twist
base_rounds.image_prompt: Dramatic unexpected moment on the Shark Tank India stage, surprised expressions on investors and entrepreneur, visual twist element with dramatic lighting change, audience gasping, cinematic tension, vibrant and dynamic illustration

ai_generation_context.context: Mid-pitch on Shark Tank India. The entrepreneur has been pitching to 5 sharks and something unexpected happens that tests their ability to think on their feet. Include Indian startup ecosystem context and Shark Tank drama.

base_rounds.title: The Offers
base_rounds.story: The moment of truth arrives. The sharks who are interested begin making their offers — but each one comes with strings attached. One offers the most money but wants a huge equity stake. Another offers strategic value but less cash. A third wants a board seat and monthly reporting. The numbers fly fast and your head spins. This is where deals are made or broken.
base_rounds.goal: Evaluate and respond to shark offers strategically
base_rounds.image_prompt: Multiple Shark Tank investors simultaneously holding up offer cards with different numbers and terms, entrepreneur in the center weighing options, split-screen showing different deal structures, money symbols and equity percentages floating in the air, high-stakes negotiation atmosphere, vibrant cinematic illustration

choices.label: Accept the highest money offer
choices.description: Go for maximum capital — take the shark offering the most money regardless of other terms
choices.feedback: You went for the money. The winning shark smiles wide. But you've given up a significant chunk of your company. Sometimes the biggest check isn't the best deal.

choices.label: Accept the strategic partner offer
choices.description: Choose the shark whose industry expertise and network will add the most long-term value
choices.feedback: You chose value over valuation. The strategic partner's network, mentorship, and industry access could be worth 10x the money. Smart founders optimize for learning, not just capital.

choices.label: Counter-offer: ask for a combination deal
choices.description: Boldly propose that multiple sharks join forces and invest together
choices.feedback: Bold move! Asking multiple sharks to combine forces is rare and risky — but when it works, you get the best of all worlds. The sharks look at each other, intrigued.

choices.label: Walk away — your terms or nothing
choices.description: Reject all offers and back yourself. You believe your company is worth more than what's on the table.
choices.feedback: The ultimate gamble. You turn your back on the sharks and walk toward the door. Will a shark chase you, or will you leave empty-handed? The studio audience gasps.

base_rounds.title: The Final Negotiation
base_rounds.story: You're in the final stretch. The terms are being hammered out word by word. Every clause matters — equity percentage, board seats, anti-dilution rights, mentorship commitments. The cameras are rolling and millions will watch this moment. The shark across from you extends a hand. Do you shake it, or push for more?
base_rounds.goal: Close the deal on the best possible terms
base_rounds.image_prompt: Close-up of a handshake moment on the Shark Tank India stage, entrepreneur and investor reaching across to shake hands, contract papers visible on a table, other sharks watching the final moment, dramatic golden lighting, emotional and climactic atmosphere, cinematic illustration
base_rounds.timeout_feedback: Your hesitation costs you dearly! The shark takes your silence as indecision and adds unfavorable terms to the deal. You've lost negotiating leverage.

choices.label: Lock it in immediately
choices.description: Shake hands and seal the deal right now before anything changes
choices.feedback: You sealed the deal! Handshakes all around. The studio audience erupts in applause. A deal done is better than a perfect deal never closed.

choices.label: Push for better terms one last time
choices.description: Make one final counter-offer to squeeze out better terms before closing
choices.feedback: A risky final push. The shark pauses, recalculates, and stares you down. The entire studio holds its breath...

choices.label: Ask for mentorship clause
choices.description: Request a formal mentorship commitment — weekly calls, introductions, and strategic guidance
choices.feedback: The shark agrees to a structured mentorship program. Ananya offers monthly brand strategy sessions. Vikram commits to tech advisory. Mentorship from a shark can be worth more than the money.

choices.label: Request performance-based equity release
choices.description: Propose that equity vests based on hitting milestones — less dilution if you perform
choices.feedback: A sophisticated deal structure that impresses everyone in the room. Performance-based equity shows you're confident in your ability to deliver results.

base_rounds.title: Post-Tank Aftermath
base_rounds.story: The cameras stop rolling. You walk offstage, legs trembling with adrenaline. Your phone is already buzzing with notifications — WhatsApp groups are going crazy, LinkedIn messages are flooding in. The episode hasn't aired yet, but word has spread through the startup grapevine. What you do in the next 48 hours will determine whether the Shark Tank effect catapults your startup or fizzles out.
base_rounds.goal: Leverage the Shark Tank momentum for maximum impact
base_rounds.image_prompt: Entrepreneur walking offstage from Shark Tank into a flurry of activity, phone buzzing with notifications, supporters cheering, media cameras flashing, transition from studio to the real world of startup building, split scene showing both the TV stage and a bustling startup office, energetic and forward-looking illustration

choices.label: Focus on scaling operations
choices.description: Use the funding and momentum to rapidly scale production, hiring, and distribution
choices.feedback: You hit the ground running. New hires, expanded warehouse, optimized supply chain. The Shark Tank money is being deployed strategically. Your shark investor sends an approving thumbs up.

choices.label: Launch a massive PR campaign
choices.description: Capitalize on the Shark Tank buzz with a coordinated media and social media blitz
choices.feedback: The Shark Tank effect multiplies exponentially with your PR push. Podcasts, newspaper interviews, Instagram reels — you're everywhere. Brand awareness skyrockets.

choices.label: Double down on product development
choices.description: Invest heavily in R&D to ensure the product lives up to the massive hype
choices.feedback: While others chase PR, you quietly build. Version 2.0 launches with features that blow customers away. The product speaks louder than any headline.

choices.label: Start preparing for Series A
choices.description: Use the Shark Tank credibility to immediately begin conversations with Series A investors
choices.feedback: You're already thinking three steps ahead. Series A deck is ready, warm intros are being made, and top-tier VCs are taking your calls. The Shark Tank stamp of approval opens every door.

crisis_events.title: Shark Walks Out!
crisis_events.description: One of the sharks suddenly slams their notebook shut and says 'I'm out!' dramatically. The energy in the room shifts instantly. The audience murmurs. The remaining sharks exchange glances. Your pitch just lost one potential investor — how you handle this moment defines your composure.
crisis_events.image_prompt: A Shark Tank investor dramatically standing up and walking away from their chair, other investors looking surprised, entrepreneur standing firm on stage, dramatic studio lighting creating tension, cinematic moment illustration

choices.label: Ignore and continue confidently
choices.description: Don't acknowledge the walkout — keep your pitch flowing without missing a beat
choices.feedback: You don't even blink. The remaining sharks respect your composure. Not every investor is the right fit, and showing you know that is a power move.

choices.label: Address their concern directly
choices.description: Turn to the departing shark and ask what would change their mind
choices.feedback: Bold move. The shark pauses at the door. Your willingness to face rejection head-on shows maturity. They sit back down, intrigued by your resilience.

crisis_events.title: Technical Malfunction!
crisis_events.description: Your product demo crashes on live television! The screen goes blank, the app freezes, and an error message pops up for all to see. Sharks raise their eyebrows. The audience shifts uncomfortably. Every founder's worst nightmare is playing out in real-time.
crisis_events.image_prompt: Product demo screen showing an error message and crash on the Shark Tank stage, entrepreneur looking at a frozen tablet with concern, investors raising eyebrows skeptically, blue screen of death visible, tense technical failure moment, dramatic illustration

choices.label: Laugh it off and improvise
choices.description: Use humor to defuse the tension and pivot to a whiteboard explanation
choices.feedback: Your quick wit saves the moment! The sharks laugh with you, not at you. Tech glitches happen to the best — how you recover shows your character as a founder.

choices.label: Have backup demo ready
choices.description: Pull out a pre-recorded video demo from your phone as a backup
choices.feedback: Always have a Plan B! The backup demo plays flawlessly. The sharks are impressed by your preparedness. Vikram nods — a founder who plans for failure is one who succeeds.

crisis_events.title: Breaking News: Competitor Funded!
crisis_events.description: Deepa Iyer casually mentions she just saw on her phone that your direct competitor raised ₹50 Crores last week from a top-tier VC. The other sharks look at you with raised eyebrows. 'How do you differentiate from them?' Priya asks pointedly. The room suddenly feels smaller.
crisis_events.image_prompt: Shark Tank investor showing a phone screen with competitor funding news to the entrepreneur, breaking news ticker visible, other investors looking skeptical, entrepreneur standing their ground, tense revelation moment on TV stage, dramatic illustration

choices.label: Highlight your unique moat
choices.description: Explain exactly what makes you defensible and why money alone can't replicate your advantage
choices.feedback: You articulate your competitive moat with precision — proprietary technology, network effects, and a brand that money can't buy. The sharks lean back, satisfied.

choices.label: Pivot the conversation to your metrics
choices.description: Redirect focus to your superior unit economics and customer retention rates
choices.feedback: Smart redirect. Your metrics tell a story that competitors' fundraising headlines cannot. Vikram appreciates the data-driven response.

crisis_events.title: Viral Social Media Moment!
crisis_events.description: Someone in the studio audience live-tweeted a killer quote from your pitch and it's gone viral! #SharkTankIndia is trending on Twitter. The sharks notice their phones buzzing with notifications. The energy in the room shifts as everyone realizes this episode is going to be special.
crisis_events.image_prompt: Shark Tank India stage with social media notifications and trending hashtags floating in the air, phones buzzing, audience members recording on smartphones, entrepreneur looking surprised and excited, Twitter trending panel visible, electric viral moment atmosphere, vibrant illustration

choices.label: Use it as leverage for better terms
choices.description: Point out that your brand value just multiplied — the deal terms should reflect this new reality
choices.feedback: You capitalize on the moment beautifully. 'That trending hashtag just made this company worth more,' you say with a confident smile. The sharks can't argue with real-time market validation.

choices.label: Stay humble and focused
choices.description: Acknowledge the buzz but keep the conversation on the deal fundamentals
choices.feedback: Your humility in a viral moment speaks volumes about your character. Rajesh says, 'This one has their feet on the ground.' True entrepreneurs don't let hype distract from substance.

interdependencies.message: Low investor confidence is tanking your pitch score! The sharks' disinterest is rattling you.
Strong product readiness is boosting investor confidence! A solid product speaks for itself.
Giving away too much equity is diluting your valuation! The sharks smell desperation.
Your excellent pitch is winning the sharks over! Confidence breeds confidence.

endings.title: Shark Tank Legend 🦈
endings.message: All sharks fought over your deal! You secured the biggest investment in Shark Tank India history. The bidding war made headlines across every business publication in the country. Your startup is destined for unicorn status, and your episode becomes the most-watched in Shark Tank India history.

endings.title: Strategic Deal Maker 🤝
endings.message: You secured a deal with the perfect strategic partner. The shark's network, industry expertise, and mentorship will catapult your startup to the next level. It wasn't the flashiest deal, but it was the smartest. Three years later, you're the one sitting in the shark's chair.

endings.title: Funded but Diluted 💸
endings.message: You got funded, but gave away more equity than you planned. The money is good and the shark's name opens doors, but you'll need to work hard to maintain control of your own company. The lesson: in the tank, every percentage point of equity is worth fighting for.

endings.title: No Deal, But Famous 📺
endings.message: No shark invested, but your pitch went viral on social media. The exposure alone is worth millions in brand value. Your website crashes from traffic the night the episode airs. Sometimes the real deal is the brand you build along the way. Many of Shark Tank's biggest successes never got a deal on the show.

endings.title: Bootstrap Champion 💪
endings.message: You walked away from all offers to bootstrap your company on your own terms. With your product this strong, you don't need their money — you need their respect, and you earned it. The sharks applaud as you leave, knowing they'll regret not investing when you're a ₹100 crore company.

random_events.title: Audience Reaction
random_events.description: The studio audience gasps at your product reveal! Spontaneous applause breaks out, and even the usually stoic camera operators are smiling. The sharks notice the audience energy.

random_events.title: Camera Close-up
random_events.description: The director calls for a dramatic close-up on your face. Every micro-expression will be broadcast to millions. The red light on the camera blinks inches from your nose. The pressure intensifies.

glossary_terms.definition: Best Alternative To a Negotiated Agreement — your fallback if no deal is reached.
glossary_terms.example: If you can't agree on a price, you could sell to a different buyer — that's your BATNA.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: A strong BATNA gives negotiating power. Knowing both parties' BATNAs reveals who needs the deal more.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: A job applicant with another offer has a stronger BATNA and can negotiate more confidently.

glossary_terms.definition: Finding solutions where both parties gain value rather than one side winning at the other's expense.
glossary_terms.example: Agreeing on a payment plan that works for both buyer and seller, rather than a discount that hurts profit.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Integrative negotiation expands the 'pie' by identifying trade-offs where each party values things differently.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Labor-management negotiations that increase productivity in exchange for better wages can benefit both sides.

glossary_terms.definition: Setting an initial reference point in a negotiation that influences the final outcome.
glossary_terms.example: The first price mentioned in a negotiation becomes the anchor around which all counteroffers are compared.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research shows people are heavily influenced by the first number they hear, even when irrelevant.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Salary negotiations: starting with a high number tends to result in higher final offers.

coaching_moment: Step into the Shark Tank! Pitch your startup to 5 legendary investors. Every shark has different priorities — convince them all or secure the deal of a lifetime.
cultural_context: Shark Tank India has become a cultural phenomenon, introducing millions of Indian viewers to the dynamics of investor pitching and venture evaluation. This game develops the entrepreneurial communication and due-diligence skills that India's growing startup generation needs.
reflection_prompt: How did you adapt as the AI shifted strategies? Which adaptation worked best?
